actions.body: Modern autonomous scientific discovery requires more than effective prediction; it necessitates a commitment to explicit falsification as the bedrock of validity. Popperian methodology, which prizes bold conjectures coupled with austerity in refutations, provides a robust framework for designing AIGS agents. By incorporating specialized agents tasked solely with falsification, we bridge the gap between speculative generation and verified scientific knowledge. As demonstrated by emerging architectures, this 'falsification agent' role allows systems to move from unproven conjectures to corroborated scientific laws, effectively minimizing the reliance on pre-existing data biases and establishing a new standard for internal model validation.
actions.lede: Integrating Popperian methodology into autonomous agents to move beyond mere pattern recognition toward rigorous scientific inquiry.
actions.reason: Provides public synthesis of collected evidence to solidify the conceptual foundation of the project.
